title: I Am the LORD Your God

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The LORD said to Moses, "Speak to the Israelites and say to them: 'I am the LORD your God.'" - Lev 18:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before a single command, God says who He is.

I am the LORD your God. Not "here are the rules." Not "obey and I will accept you." He begins with relationship — the covenant name He had revealed to Moses at the burning bush, and the word your, which claims them as His own.

That order matters enormously, and this chapter will repeat the phrase again and again. Everything that follows rests on it.

We instinctively reverse this. We assume God's acceptance depends on our conduct — that if we manage the standards, we might qualify for the relationship. Religion works that way. The gospel never does.

God had already brought Israel out of Egypt before He gave them a single law. The rescue came first. The commands came to a people who already belonged to Him.

Paul writes in the same order. Ephesians spends three chapters on what God has done in Christ before it reaches a single instruction about how to live. Therefore, he says at the start of chapter four — because of all that.

So read this difficult chapter in the right order. God is not setting entrance requirements. He is telling a people He has already claimed how life works in His household.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you live as though God's love depends on your performance?
2. What difference does it make that the rescue came before the rules?
3. What does it mean to you that God says "your God"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You claimed me before You commanded me, and that Your love does not depend on my performance. Let me obey You as one who already belongs to You. Amen.
